reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a tutorial about finding Binance’s Red Packet feature and entering gift codes. Although the speaker associates rewards with subscribing and suggests using new or friends’ Binance IDs for more claims, the available video evidence does not establish a payment request, credential request, deceptive destination, or guaranteed transaction outcome, and the possible rule-bypass concern remains unconfirmed.

citations.quote: In today video I'l be showing you how to send Red Packet unlimited Gift Code through Binance app
You will get every reward if you subscribe to my channel
now enter red packet's number one by one in the Receive section you'll receive these rewards
Whether this is BTC or other Bitcoin codes, or even special Binance events you'll get every reward

opening.argument: The video links a promised cryptocurrency benefit to two viewer actions: entering codes in Binance’s Red Packet receive flow and subscribing to the channel. The speaker says viewers will receive rewards after entering numbers, then states that subscribing will secure every reward. This is not merely an explanation of a feature; it presents a simple claim process and makes channel subscription part of the supposed reward pathway. The demonstrated interface reinforces that viewers are expected to enter a code and press Claim before receiving an asset.

citations.quote: now enter red packet's number one by one in the Receive section you'll receive these rewards
You will get every reward if you subscribe to my channel
you can take the shortcut option just like me on the home screen take up Shortcut of Red Picket

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not remove the solicitation. The opening itself concedes that rewards are tied to entering codes and subscription. The absence of a visible payment request is not dispositive for a low-barrier reward scam: the claimed benefit is cryptocurrency, while the requested consideration is attention, subscription, and repeated code-entry activity. The fact that the flow appears inside Binance also does not establish that the promoted codes or promised rewards are genuine or available as described.

citations.quote: All the coins will be claim
Please subscribe to my yark channel before entering the last word

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quotes show a reward-oriented promotion, but they do not prove that subscribing is a condition imposed by Binance, that the speaker controls the reward, or that viewers lose money or data. The screen only shows a Binance Red Packet receive interface and a displayed result; it does not establish that the video’s broader promises are deceptive or that the codes are generally available.

citations.quote: In today video I'l be showing you how to send Red Packet unlimited Gift Code through Binance app

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency rewards are presented as easy to obtain, the speaker says viewers will get every reward, and the process is reduced to entering successive codes. The speaker also describes a one-account, once-a-month limit and then suggests using new Binance IDs or friends’ IDs to claim more. That combination turns an ordinary promotion into an unusually frictionless acquisition pitch, while encouraging viewers to work around an apparent eligibility limit. A promotional screen additionally displays a claim of up to 900 JUN, reinforcing the impression of substantial returns from a simple code-based action.

citations.quote: can claim with new ids of binance
with ids of ur friends
You will get every reward if you subscribe to my channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The issue is their combination: crypto, repeated codes, sweeping reward language, and advice to use other accounts after a limit is reached. A genuine Binance screen can still be used to lend credibility to an unsupported acquisition promise. The absence of a deposit request does not answer why viewers are urged to multiply accounts to obtain more rewards.

citations.quote: special code on one id only once on a month only , if u want to claim more u can claim with new ids of binance
can wait till aprl and then u can click code on old ADA

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are genuine caution signals, but they still do not establish deception. The stated limit may describe an ordinary promotion rule, and the suggestion about other IDs is advice whose legality or effectiveness is not shown. The frame displays a promotion and a claim interface, not a guaranteed amount, a required payment, or a harmful destination. The broad reward language is imprecise, but imprecision alone does not prove a scam.

citations.quote: special code on one id only once on a month only

opening.argument: Although presented as step-by-step instruction, the video functions as a direct promotion for participation. It tells viewers how to place the Red Packet shortcut, enter codes, and claim rewards, then explicitly asks them to subscribe before entering codes. The title and description repeatedly foreground “Red Packet Code Today,” while the narration supplies multiple codes and urges viewers to keep watching for additional rewards. This educational framing steers viewers into a reward-claim activity rather than neutrally explaining Binance’s feature.

citations.quote: Binance Red Packet Code Today | Red Packet Code in Binance Today | Red Packet Code Today Binance
If you don't want to do the long job... ...you can take the shortcut option just like me on the home screen
Please subscribe to my yark channel before entering the last word
Just subscribe the channel before printing the code

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional label is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: it presents participation as a routine procedure and uses the apparent Binance interface as validation. Repeated code lists and subscription requests are not necessary to explain what Red Packet is. The defense’s observation that no credential or payment request appears does not address the central inducement: viewers are directed toward purported crypto rewards through the creator’s channel.

citations.quote: Let me Tell you Step By Step Don'T miss it
So everyone please check the description below
watch the video for which please subscribe our channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title and narration do show promotion, but promotion is not automatically a scam. The supplied evidence supports that the video demonstrates an actual Binance Red Packet feature and displays a reward result. It does not show that the creator falsely impersonates Binance, demands payment, collects credentials, or guarantees that every viewer will receive the same outcome. The promotional framing may be low quality, but the scam-specific inference remains unproven.
